notes.title: How the cuisine filters were policed
notes.body: Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. San Francisco’s signature strength is its food canon: the Mission burrito and taqueria belt, Cantonese dim sum in the oldest Chinatown in America, cioppino and Dungeness crab, Tenderloin Vietnamese, the Bay’s famous Burmese, sourdough and the third-wave coffee it helped invent — each led by Michelin, The Infatuation, KQED and the SF Standard. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

places.n: SFO Louis A. Turpen Aviation Museum & Library
places.ad: International Terminal Main Hall, Departures Level (pre-security), San Francisco International Airport, San Francisco, CA 94128
places.w: The only accredited museum inside an airport: a free, pre-security gallery built as a replica 1930s passenger terminal, tracing West Coast and Pacific commercial aviation with aircraft models, airline memorabilia and photographs. Open daily 10am-4:30pm, no ticket needed.

places.n: Sign Hill (SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO THE INDUSTRIAL CITY letters)
places.ad: Sign Hill Park, Poplar Ave, South San Francisco, CA 94080
places.w: The city's Hollywood-style hillside sign: white concrete letters 48-65 ft tall spelling SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO THE INDUSTRIAL CITY, built in 1929 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places. A 30-acre park with ~2 miles of trails climbs to the letters and bay views.

pv.src: WIKIPEDIA (South San Francisco hillside sign published coords)

places.n: San Bruno Mountain State & County Park
places.w: A rare island of native coastal-scrub habitat rising straight off the bay's edge above Daly City, Brisbane and South SF. Summit and ridge trails deliver 360-degree views from the Golden Gate to the Santa Cruz Mountains; home to endangered Mission blue butterflies.

pv.src: WIKIPEDIA (San Bruno Mountain State Park published coords)

places.n: Sweeney Ridge (San Francisco Bay Discovery Site)
places.ad: Sneath Lane Trailhead, Sneath Ln, San Bruno, CA 94066
places.w: GGNRA ridgeline between San Bruno and Pacifica where the Portola expedition first sighted San Francisco Bay on Nov 4, 1769 - a registered historic landmark. Trails from Sneath Lane and Skyline College climb to the discovery-site monument and ocean-to-bay panoramas.

pv.src: WIKIPEDIA (San Francisco Bay Discovery Site published coords)

places.ad: 1651 Coyote Point Dr, San Mateo, CA 94401
places.w: A hands-on science-and-wildlife museum inside Coyote Point Recreation Area, overlooking the bay: live native-animal exhibits (raptors, foxes, bobcat) and interactive natural-science galleries. Surrounded by shoreline, eucalyptus groves and beach in a regional park.

places.n: San Mateo Central Park & Japanese Garden
places.w: A hidden strolling garden designed by Nagao Sakurai of the Imperial Palace of Tokyo, with a granite pagoda, teahouse, koi pond and bamboo grove, tucked inside downtown San Mateo's Central Park. Free admission.

places.ad: Beach Blvd (at Santa Rosa Ave), Pacifica, CA 94044
places.w: A 1,140-ft concrete pier jutting into the Pacific off Sharp Park Beach - a free, no-license fishing and crabbing spot famous for salmon and Dungeness crab runs, with wide-open sunset and whale-watching views straight out over the ocean.

places.ad: Devil's Slide Trail, CA-1 (Cabrillo Hwy), Pacifica, CA 94044
places.w: A 1.3-mile paved clifftop trail on a former stretch of Highway 1, reopened in 2014 after the Tom Lantos Tunnels rerouted the road. It hugs a sheer cliff face hundreds of feet above the surf with sweeping ocean, seabird and gray-whale views. Parking lots at both ends.

A 110-acre GGNRA headland in Pacifica: a short climb up the Mori Point Peak loop delivers a dramatic bluff-top view over the ocean, Sharp Park Beach and the coastline, through wildflower meadows and wetlands that shelter the endangered red-legged frog and San Francisco garter snake.

The point where the San Andreas Fault meets the Pacific - the closest land to the epicenter of the 1906 earthquake, its tarmac visibly rippled by the fault. Cliffside 'laminar flow' winds make it one of the Bay Area's premier hang-gliding and paragliding launches, with big coastal sunsets.

pv.src: GOOGLEMAPS park parking lot (end of Westline Dr)

places.n: Burlingame Museum of PEZ Memorabilia — CLOSED
places.w: A beloved roadside oddity that displayed one of the world's largest PEZ dispenser collections plus banned/rare pieces and the 'world's largest PEZ dispenser.' Permanently closed in July 2019 - kept here for the record; do not visit.

pv.ss: Yelp marked CLOSED + Wikipedia: permanently closed July 2019

places.ad: Golden Gate Bridge, San Francisco, CA 94129
places.w: The 1937 Art Deco suspension span in International Orange is SF's defining icon; the free Welcome Center and south vista point at Strauss Plaza sit at the city end for the classic view and a walk across the deck.
places.k: Welcome Center open daily 9am-5pm; walkway free, southbound toll on drivers only.

places.w: The former federal penitentiary in the middle of the bay, now a Golden Gate NRA site with the audio-guided cellhouse tour, gardens and the 1969 occupation history; ferries depart Pier 33 Alcatraz Landing.
places.k: Book the City Experiences ferry well ahead - tickets sell out weeks out. A short dock repair briefly closed the island in April 2026; normal service resumed.

places.ad: Powell Street cable car turnaround, Powell St & Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102
places.w: The world's last manually operated cable-car system, running since 1873; the Powell-Hyde and Powell-Mason lines climb Nob and Russian hills from the Powell/Market turnaround down to Fisherman's Wharf.
places.k: A sheave-rehab project (Feb-Jun 2026) causes occasional segment closures with bus shuttles; at least one line stays running.

places.w: Free museum inside the still-working Nob Hill powerhouse, where you can watch the giant sheaves and cables that haul every cable car in the city, plus antique cars and exhibits.
places.k: Free. Closed Mondays.

places.w: The 1898 Beaux-Arts ferry terminal with its landmark clock tower, reborn as a food hall of local artisans; the Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday farmers' market on the plaza is one of the country's best.

places.ad: Jefferson St & Taylor St, San Francisco, CA 94133
places.w: The historic Italian fishing port turned waterfront district; walk-up crab and clam-chowder stands line Jefferson Street, and the iconic 1968 crab-wheel sign marks its heart at Taylor and Jefferson.

places.ad: Beach St & The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA 94133
places.w: A 45-acre waterfront complex of shops and restaurants best known for the wild California sea lions that have hauled out on K-Dock since 1990, barking and jockeying for space for free.

places.ad: 1 Telegraph Hill Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94133
places.w: The 210-ft fluted tower atop Telegraph Hill, wrapped inside with free 1934 WPA Depression-era murals of California life; climb the flower-lined wooden Filbert Steps up to it for 360-degree bay views.
places.k: Ground-floor murals free; elevator to the observation deck about $10.

places.ad: Lombard St between Hyde St & Leavenworth St, San Francisco, CA 94109
places.w: The one-way brick block on Russian Hill with eight hairpin turns added in 1922 to tame the grade, lined with hydrangea beds; free to walk down the side stairs or drive one-way eastbound.
places.k: GPS to 1070 Lombard St. Free, open 24/7.

pv.src: WIKIPEDIA (published coords) / Apple Maps place pin

places.w: The 'Postcard Row' of seven Queen Anne Victorians on Steiner Street, framed against the downtown skyline from Alamo Square Park - among the most photographed houses in America.

places.ad: Dragon Gate, Grant Ave & Bush St, San Francisco, CA 94108
places.w: The 1970 Dragon Gate at Grant and Bush, a Taiwan gift with guardian lions, is the southern entrance to the oldest Chinatown in North America; Grant Avenue and lantern-strung Ross Alley run north from it.

SF's tallest and most recognizable tower (1972), reopened in 2024 after a $1B restoration; the adjoining half-acre Transamerica Redwood Park, a public grove of coast redwoods with a sculpture, is the free draw.
places.k: Tower interior is private offices; Redwood Park is the public space.

places.ad: 900 North Point St, San Francisco, CA 94109
places.w: The 1893 red-brick Ghirardelli chocolate factory, now a landmark open-air complex of shops and restaurants above Aquatic Park; the original Ghirardelli ice-cream and chocolate shop still serves hot-fudge sundaes.

places.ad: Pier 45, Shed A, San Francisco, CA 94133
places.w: One of the world's largest collections of antique coin-operated arcade machines - 300-plus fortune tellers, player pianos, and the creepy Laffing Sal - free to enter, a quarter or two to play.
places.k: Free admission; machines take coins. Open daily.

pv.src: WIKIPEDIA (published coords) / Apple Maps place pin

places.w: A Civil War-era brick coastal fort tucked directly under the south end of the Golden Gate Bridge, with cannon casemates, a spiral staircase, and dramatic bridge-and-bay views; free.
places.k: Free. Fort interior open Fri-Mon only; grounds Thu-Mon.

places.w: The national park on Aquatic Park Cove: a free Visitor Center, the streamline-moderne Maritime Museum (900 Beach St), the curved swimming beach and bleachers, and the historic Hyde Street Pier fleet.
places.k: Hyde Street Pier is closed for the Hyde Street Rebuild and its historic ships are temporarily relocated to Mare Island; Visitor Center, Maritime Museum and Aquatic Park remain open.

places.ad: 83 Marina Green Dr (end of Yacht Rd), San Francisco, CA 94123
places.w: A wave-activated acoustic sculpture (1986) on a jetty past the Golden Gate Yacht Club, built by Exploratorium artists from salvaged cemetery granite; 25 PVC-and-concrete pipes murmur with the tides.
places.k: Free, always open; best at high tide.

places.ad: Pier 7, The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA 94111
places.w: An 840-ft public promenade pier with antique iron lamp posts and wooden benches jutting into the bay; a favorite for anglers and photographers - the deck lines up straight at the Transamerica Pyramid.
places.k: Free, open to pedestrians and fishing.

places.ad: 50 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118
places.w: Golden Gate Park's fine-arts museum for American art, textiles and global cultures, wrapped in a copper Herzog & de Meuron building with a free 9th-floor observation tower over the park. Open Tue-Sun; one ticket also admits the Legion of Honor same day.

A neoclassical palace on the Lincoln Park cliffs (a Beaux-Arts copy of Paris's Legion of Honor) holding European painting and Rodin bronzes, with Lands End and Golden Gate views out front. Open Tue-Sun; admission covers same-day de Young entry.

places.ad: 55 Music Concourse Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118
places.w: A natural-history museum, aquarium, planetarium and four-story indoor rainforest under one living roof in Golden Gate Park. A top family stop; open daily with Sunday opening at 11am.

places.ad: 75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118
places.w: The oldest public Japanese garden in the US (1894), with a drum bridge, pagoda, koi ponds and a tea house; the birthplace of the American fortune cookie. Free entry Mon/Wed/Fri 9-10am.

places.ad: 100 John F Kennedy Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118
places.w: A gleaming white Victorian glasshouse (1879), the oldest wood-and-glass conservatory in North America, packed with tropical and aquatic plants. Open Thu-Tue; closed Wednesdays for maintenance.
55 acres and roughly 8,000 kinds of plants in Golden Gate Park, from a cloud-forest collection to a magnolia grove that's one of the best outside China. Open daily.
places.k: Free for SF residents with ID; paid for non-residents.

places.n: Dutch Windmill & Queen Wilhelmina Tulip Garden
places.ad: 1690 John F Kennedy Dr, San Francisco, CA 94121
places.w: A 1903 Dutch-style windmill at Golden Gate Park's ocean edge, fronted by the Queen Wilhelmina tulip garden that blooms brightest in late winter and early spring. Free, open grounds.

places.ad: 680 Point Lobos Ave, San Francisco, CA 94121
places.w: A rugged NPS coastal trail past cypress groves, shipwreck-strewn surf and the concrete ruins of the 1896 Sutro Baths, with the Golden Gate Bridge framed the whole way. Free; open daily.
places.k: The adjacent Cliff House (1090 Point Lobos Ave) has been closed since 2020; a reopening has been announced for late 2026 but repeatedly delayed.

places.ad: 16th Ave & Moraga St, San Francisco, CA 94122
places.w: A 163-step mosaic staircase in Golden Gate Heights, tiled in a sea-to-stars swirl by artists Aileen Barr and Colette Crutcher with the neighborhood; climb it to Grand View Park for a Sunset-and-ocean panorama. Free, always open.

pv.src: WIKIPEDIA published coords / Apple Maps place pin

places.w: The West Coast's flagship modern-art museum, expanded by Snohetta into seven gallery floors with a free ground-floor Richard Serra and a living wall on the sculpture terrace. Open daily except Wednesday.
One of the largest Asian art collections in the West, 18,000+ works spanning 6,000 years, housed in the old Beaux-Arts main library on Civic Center. Open Thu-Mon; closed Tue/Wed.
Daniel Libeskind's tilted blue-steel cube grafted onto a 1907 power substation, one of downtown's boldest buildings.
places.k: CLOSED as an operating museum since December 2024 amid a financial crisis; in March 2026 the museum announced it is selling the Libeskind building, though it continues hosting some events through January 2027. The exterior remains a landmark to view.

pv.ss: Closed since Dec 2024 (finances); Libeskind building listed for sale Mar 2026 (KQED / jweekly).

places.ad: Pier 15, The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA 94111
places.w: A pioneering hands-on science and perception museum sprawling across an Embarcadero pier, with 600+ tinker-with-it exhibits and adults-only After Dark Thursday nights. Open Tue-Sun.
A cluttered shrine to the Beat Generation across from City Lights, with Kerouac and Ginsberg letters, first editions and the car from the film of On the Road.
places.k: Temporarily closed from December 2025 for a seismic (soft-story) retrofit, with reopening announced for mid-to-late 2026 - confirm before visiting.

places.w: The twin-spired "Italian Cathedral of the West" on Washington Square, where Joe DiMaggio and Marilyn Monroe took wedding photos on the steps. Open daily.
In a former Presidio barracks, the story of Walt Disney himself - early drawings, the multiplane camera, Oscars and a huge model of Disneyland. Open Thu-Mon.
A monumental Beaux-Arts rotunda and colonnade left from the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition, mirrored in a swan lagoon in the Marina. Grounds are free and open daily.
A mile of Presidio sand with a full-frontal view of the Golden Gate Bridge; the north end is clothing-optional and the surf is strong (no swimming). Free, open daily.

A 14-acre park (opened 2022) built over the Presidio Parkway tunnels, linking Crissy Field to the Main Post with Golden Gate views, a nature-play Outpost for kids and picnic meadows. Free, open daily.
A French Gothic Episcopal cathedral atop Nob Hill with gilded Ghiberti "Gates of Paradise" doors and two labyrinths you can walk. Open daily; admission for general visiting.

places.ad: Peace Plaza, Post St & Buchanan St, San Francisco, CA 94115
places.w: A five-tiered concrete stupa gifted by sister-city Osaka in 1968, the centerpiece of the Peace Plaza in one of only three remaining Japantowns in the US. Free, open plaza.
Mission San Francisco de Asis (1776), the city's oldest surviving building, with the original adobe chapel beside an ornate 1918 basilica and a historic cemetery. Open daily 9am-4pm.

places.ad: Dolores St & 19th St, San Francisco, CA 94114
places.w: The Mission's sun-trap hillside lawn, part civic living room and part downtown-skyline overlook, packed on any warm weekend. Free, open daily.

A 1922 movie-palace landmark and the heart of the Castro, famous for its Wurlitzer organ and sing-alongs. Reopened February 2026 after a $41M restoration, now with flexible seating for films and concerts.
places.k: Reopened February 2026 after a two-year renovation led by Another Planet Entertainment; programming now mixes film with concerts and events - check the calendar.

places.ad: 501 Twin Peaks Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94114
places.w: The near-geographic center of the city and its best 360-degree panorama, from downtown and the bridges to the ocean. Free; open daily 5am-midnight.

The first stand-alone museum of LGBTQ history and culture in the US, in the Castro, drawing on the GLBT Historical Society's archive (Harvey Milk material included). Open Tue-Sun; free first Wednesdays.
The densest concentration of murals in the Mission - a one-block alley off 24th Street painted since the 1970s with Latin-American political and cultural art, continuously renewed. Free, always open.

places.ad: Bernal Heights Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94110
places.w: A grassy, car-free hilltop above the Mission with a mellow local vibe and a wide-open view of downtown and the bay; a favorite dog and sunset spot. Free, open daily.

places.ad: Oracle Park (Giants ballpark), South of Market, San Francisco, CA 94107
places.w: Bayfront home of the SF Giants — the Coca-Cola bottle slide, the giant glove, McCovey Cove splash hits and the ballpark crab sandwich.
places.k: ballpark baseball waterfront

places.w: 5.4-acre rooftop park atop the Salesforce Transit Center — 600 trees, 16,000 plants, a linear fountain, a gondola and ~20 free events a week.
places.k: park rooftop garden free

pv.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transbay_Transit_Center (Wikipedia published coordinates of the Transit Center the park tops)

places.ad: Yerba Buena Gardens, SoMa, San Francisco, CA 94103
places.w: Three city blocks of gardens, public art and free concerts; walk behind the falling-water curtain of the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial.
places.k: park garden free art

places.ad: Chase Center, Mission Bay, San Francisco, CA 94158
places.w: The Warriors' arena (opened 2019) and concert venue; the surrounding Thrive City blocks carry restaurants and a bay-side plaza.
places.k: arena music venue

places.ad: Sutro Heights Park, above the Cliff House / Ocean Beach, San Francisco, CA 94121
places.w: Adolph Sutro's 1885 hilltop garden above the Cliff House — the parapet, stone wall and statue plinths, with views over Ocean Beach. Free, part of the GGNRA.
places.k: park view history free

places.ad: Tank Hill Park, Twin Peaks Blvd / end of Belgrave Ave, San Francisco, CA 94117
places.w: A 2.9-acre rocky knob in Ashbury Heights — the locals' quieter Twin Peaks, with a sweeping city panorama. Free.
places.k: view hill park free hidden gem

places.ad: Seward Mini Park, Seward St / 70 Corwin St, San Francisco, CA 94114
places.w: A pair of parallel concrete slides built into a Castro hillside mini-park — bring cardboard. Free.
places.k: oddity park free hidden gem

places.n: Blue Heron Lake (Stow Lake) & Strawberry Hill
places.ad: Blue Heron Lake (formerly Stow Lake), Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA 94118
places.w: Golden Gate Park's largest man-made lake (renamed Blue Heron Lake) — a 1-mile loop, boat rentals and the 430-ft Strawberry Hill island with its waterfall. Free to walk.
places.k: park lake garden free

pv.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strawberry_Hill_(San_Francisco) (Wikipedia published coordinates of Strawberry Hill, the lake's island)

places.ad: Crane Cove Park, Dogpatch waterfront, San Francisco, CA 94107
places.w: Seven-acre Port park in Dogpatch on the old Union Iron Works shipyard — a small public beach for kayaks and paddleboards, the historic cranes, a big playground and grills. Free.
places.k: park waterfront beach free

places.ad: Heron's Head Park, Bayview waterfront, San Francisco, CA 94124
places.w: 22-acre restored wetland on a Bayview pier spit — shoreline trails thick with migratory birds and the off-grid EcoCenter. Free.
places.k: park nature waterfront birds free

pv.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heron's_Head_Park (Wikipedia published coordinates; 3-decimal = park centroid of a 22-acre site)

places.ad: Bayview Opera House, 3rd St, Bayview, San Francisco, CA 94124
places.w: SF's oldest theater building (1888), survivor of the 1906 quake — now the Bayview's community arts hub.
places.k: theatre history landmark

places.ad: India Basin Shoreline Park, Bayview waterfront, San Francisco, CA 94124
places.w: 10-acre Bayview waterfront park (opened 2024-25) — paths, food gardens, amphitheaters and a food pavilion for chef pop-ups. Free.
places.k: park waterfront free

places.ad: Huntington Park, 1050 Taylor St, San Francisco, CA 94108
places.w: 1.3-acre Nob Hill square between Grace Cathedral and the Fairmont, centred on its Fountain of the Tortoises. Free.
places.k: park nob hill free

places.w: The 1907 grand hotel crowning Nob Hill, where the UN Charter was drafted in 1945 — lobby and view terraces open to all.
places.k: historic hotel landmark nob hill

places.ad: Macondray Lane (stairs at Taylor St), Russian Hill, San Francisco, CA 94133
places.w: Leafy two-block pedestrian lane on Russian Hill — Armistead Maupin's model for Barbary Lane in Tales of the City. Free.
places.k: hidden gem stairway lane free

places.ad: Ina Coolbrith Park, 1715 Taylor St, Russian Hill, San Francisco, CA 94133
places.w: Tiny terraced Russian Hill park with a sweeping view over the Financial District and the Bay Bridge. Free.
places.k: park view free

pv.src: mapcarta (OSM/Wikidata-derived) place page https://mapcarta.com/23063904 'Ina Coolbrith Park' 37.79823,-122.4133 (via WebSearch 2026-10-02)

places.ad: Haight St & Ashbury St, San Francisco, CA 94117
places.w: The corner where 1960s flower power blossomed — Victorian hillsides, vintage and record shops along Upper Haight.
places.k: historic district shopping music free

pv.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haight-Ashbury (Wikipedia district coordinate, 4-decimal; near the namesake corner)

places.ad: Buena Vista Park, Haight-Ashbury, San Francisco, CA 94117
places.w: SF's oldest official park (1867) — a wooded hill above the Haight with city and bay views. Free.
places.k: park view free

places.ad: Corona Heights Park (by the Randall Museum), San Francisco, CA 94114
places.w: Red-chert rock outcrop above the Castro and the Haight with a 360-degree view (and the Randall Museum at its foot). Free.
places.k: park view free

places.ad: Fort Mason Center, Marina waterfront, San Francisco, CA 94123
places.w: Former Army post turned waterfront arts and community campus between the Marina and Aquatic Park — piers, galleries, theatres and the Great Meadow. Free to wander.
places.k: waterfront history park free

places.ad: Crissy Field, Presidio, San Francisco, CA 94129
places.w: Former military airfield turned restored tidal marsh and bayfront promenade, with the Golden Gate dead ahead. Free.
places.k: park waterfront view beach free

places.ad: Alta Plaza Park, Pacific Heights, San Francisco, CA 94115
places.w: Terraced Pacific Heights hilltop park — from the top you see clear across the bay to Sausalito. Free.
places.k: park view free

places.ad: City Lights Bookstore, Columbus Ave at Jack Kerouac Alley, North Beach, San Francisco, CA 94133
places.w: Lawrence Ferlinghetti's 1953 bookstore and publisher — ground zero of the Beat movement, three floors of books and poetry.
places.k: bookstore beat history landmark

places.ad: Washington Square, North Beach (facing Saints Peter and Paul Church), San Francisco, CA 94133
places.w: North Beach's green heart under the twin spires of Saints Peter and Paul — morning tai chi, focaccia from the corner bakery. Free.
places.k: park north beach free

places.ad: Old St. Mary's Cathedral, California St, Chinatown, San Francisco, CA 94108
places.w: California's first cathedral (1854), built of granite quarried in China and brick shipped round Cape Horn, at the edge of Chinatown.
places.k: church history landmark cathedral

places.ad: Ocean Beach, western edge of the Sunset/Richmond, San Francisco, CA
places.w: Seven miles of wild Pacific sand on the city's western edge, from the Cliff House to Fort Funston — big surf, bonfire rings, sunsets. Free.
places.k: beach waterfront view free

places.ad: Fort Funston, southwest San Francisco coast (GGNRA), San Francisco, CA
places.w: Wind-scoured coastal bluffs where hang-gliders launch over the Pacific; sandy trails down to the beach. Free (GGNRA).
places.k: view park beach free

places.ad: San Francisco Zoo & Gardens, by Ocean Beach, Sunset District, San Francisco, CA
places.w: Northern California's largest zoo, by Ocean Beach.
places.k: zoo family animals

places.ad: Sigmund Stern Recreation Grove, Sunset District, San Francisco, CA
places.w: 33-acre eucalyptus-and-redwood dell whose free summer Stern Grove Festival concerts draw throngs.
places.k: park music concerts free

places.ad: Clarion Alley, between Mission & Valencia, 17th & 18th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
places.w: The Clarion Alley Mural Project's open-air gallery — 700+ murals since 1992 on social, economic and environmental justice. Free.
places.k: murals art free

pv.src: Atlas Obscura place page https://www.atlasobscura.com/places/clarion-alley published coords 37.76298,-122.4206 via WebSearch 2026-10-02

places.w: Women-led community centre (1979) wrapped in the MaestraPeace mural honouring women leaders and artists worldwide.
places.k: murals art landmark free

places.ad: Harvey Milk Plaza, Market St / Castro St / 17th St, San Francisco, CA 94114
places.w: Memorial plaza to Harvey Milk at the Castro's crossroads — under the giant rainbow flag, the entrance to Castro station.
places.k: history LGBTQ landmark free

places.ad: Mount Davidson Park, San Francisco, CA
places.w: The city's highest natural point (928 ft) — a 1.5-mile forest loop to the historic Mount Davidson Cross.
places.k: hike view park free

places.ad: Glen Canyon Park, Glen Park, San Francisco, CA
places.w: 70-acre wild canyon with rock outcrops and a creek in the middle of the city. Free.
places.k: park hike nature free

places.ad: San Francisco City Hall, Van Ness Ave, Civic Center, San Francisco, CA 94102
places.w: Beaux-Arts City Hall on Van Ness Avenue, the grand centrepiece of the Civic Center.
places.k: architecture landmark history free

places.ad: Union Square, Downtown, San Francisco, CA 94108
places.w: The 2.6-acre plaza at the heart of the shopping and hotel district, ringed by department stores. Free.
places.k: shopping square landmark free

places.ad: Maiden Lane, off Union Square, San Francisco, CA 94108
places.w: Pedestrian-only alley off Union Square — once a notorious red-light street, now boutiques and cocktail bars. Free.
places.k: shopping hidden gem history free

places.ad: Lotta's Fountain, Market St / Geary St / Kearny St, San Francisco, CA 94103
places.w: 1875 cast-iron fountain where survivors of the 1906 earthquake used to meet — said to be haunted by them still. Free.
places.k: history landmark oddity free

places.ad: 2 New Montgomery St, San Francisco, CA 94105
places.w: The 1875 Palace (rebuilt 1909 after the quake) — step into the Garden Court under 80,000 panes of stained glass.
places.k: historic hotel architecture landmark

places.ad: Old San Francisco Mint, SoMa, San Francisco, CA
places.w: Greek Revival landmark (1874) that minted gold coins until 1937 — now used for exhibitions and events.

places.w: Chinatown's group-dinner institution since 1985, built around live salt-and-pepper crab chopped and fried in the shell. Nine straight years of Michelin recognition; The Infatuation's go-to for a Cantonese banquet.

Chinatown's fiery Sichuan standard-bearer and a Michelin Bib Gourmand every year since 2012. Nearly every plate is crowned with chilies — get the 'explosive' fried chicken and the chili-oil bean-jelly noodles.

A Chinatown-edge institution since 1988 (chef Kathy Fang of 'Chef Dynasty'), famous for letting the staff order for you. Time Out's pick: the cold sesame noodles; the signature Nanking sesame chicken and peanut-sauce potstickers.
Old-school Chinatown Cantonese with live seafood tanks and 80-plus daily dim sum items — the spot Obama famously ordered takeout from. Go for the tank lobster and cilantro shrimp dumplings.

places.w: Outer Richmond glam-dim-sum from the Koi Palace family — creative XLB in squid-ink, black-truffle and beet wrappers by day, Cantonese hot pot by night. Order the 'Five Guys' soup-dumpling flight.
Inner Sunset Shandong-style/Korean-Chinese cult favorite whose sweet-garlicky dry-fried chicken wings are a citywide obsession (a former Bib Gourmand). Pair them with the handmade black-bean noodles.

The cult of Northern-Vietnamese chicken pho, reborn in the Financial District in 2025 after the original Tenderloin flagship closed. Hanoi-style phở gà — no anise, no bean sprouts, just clean broth. Also try the stir-fried pho.

Matthew Ho's modern Northern-Vietnamese follow-up to his family's Bodega Bistro, bringing casual fine-dining to the Tenderloin edge. Order the bún chả, garlic noodles and shaking beef; there's a tasting menu with caviar bánh khọt.
Cash-only Tenderloin counter that The Infatuation and Time Out both crown for the best bánh mì in SF — crackly rolls, well-seasoned proteins, packed to bursting, about $5. Get the combination.

A chefs'-favorite Tenderloin Thai (since 2008) with a novel-length menu of regional dishes — including rabbit, frog and venison — beyond the usual. A former Bib Gourmand; get the garlic pork and roasted-duck curry.

places.ad: 55 Cyril Magnin St, San Francisco, CA 94102
places.w: Pim Techamuanvivit's Michelin-recognized Thai off Union Square, using local farm ingredients — the slow-cooked green rabbit curry with meatballs is the signature. No pad-Thai-by-default here; deeply regional cooking.
The Inner Richmond original (since 1992) that made Bay Area Burmese famous — its tossed-tableside fermented tea-leaf salad is a cult classic. No reservations; expect a line.
SF's oldest Burmese restaurant (est. 1984) and a 2024 James Beard 'America's Classic' honoree. The Richmond-District standard for tea-leaf salad and Burmese home cooking.
The Mission's more elegant sibling to Burma Superstar, serving the same Burmese classics — the Good Food Award-winning tea-leaf salad in a sleeker space. Named among SFGATE's best Burmese for 2025.

places.ad: 1581 Webster St Suite 235, San Francisco, CA 94115
places.w: Japantown's benchmark for Hakata-style ramen — a 20-hour milky tonkotsu broth with ultra-thin noodles and melting chashu; The Infatuation and Time Out both rate it a top SF bowl. Try the chicken paitan too.

Sylvan Mishima Brackett's redwood-and-hinoki izakaya, a Michelin Bib Gourmand, plating handmade Japanese izakaya fare with NorCal produce. Get the binchotan-grilled tsukune and sansho-pepper chicken wings.

Chris Oh's Inner Sunset Korean spot (a former Michelin star) with a tree-shaded patio and '90s hip-hop soundtrack — grill-it-yourself bulgogi, pork belly and 48-hour marinated kalbi, plus creamy pickled quail eggs.

SF's first Filipino fine-dining restaurant (Fisherman's Wharf), a Michelin-recognized standout for contemporary Filipino cooking. Order the pork-belly adobo with pineapple, lumpia and sisig fried rice.

places.w: SF's third-wave standard-bearer; the Ferry Building espresso bar is the only Blue Bottle pouring single-origin flights (the original Mint Plaza cafe is now closed).
One of the original SF third-wave roasters; the cavernous Valencia flagship is a Mission daily ritual, cited in Food & Wine's 2026 top U.S. coffee-cities ranking.
Iconic SoMa roastery in a 1914 warehouse open to the rafters; craft light-roast single origins roasted on-site, one of the shops that gave SF its roaster depth.
Mission third-wave roaster (est. 2008) roasting in-house on a vintage German machine; a spare menu that lets the roast talk, with a visible roaster and long communal tables.
Russian Hill/Polk Gulch's sleekest cafe, a Scandi-minimalist counter; the owner's obsessive sourcing from Guatemala, Kenya and Honduras and its housemade nut milk draw the coffee crowd.
Outer Sunset roaster-bakery (est. 2014); the signature Snowy Plover is a foggy-day icon of the neighborhood coffee scene.
Cow Hollow micro-cafe from Trish Rothgeb — the roaster who literally coined 'third wave coffee' — and Nicholas Cho; pineapple-wallpaper #pineappleselfie spot with a custom pour-over bar.
Mission cocktail landmark whose art-object menus reinvent around a theme (Pantone colors, astrology, records); a World's 50 Best Bars regular and top-ranked U.S. bar.
Hayes Valley tiki temple with the largest rum selection in the U.S. (1,300+) and 80 cocktails; six-time World's 50 Best Bars listee and once Tales of the Cocktail's best U.S. bar.
Tenderloin Prohibition-era speakeasy in a real 1920s bar space; password-and-buzzer entry, five secret rooms, and the walk-in Library behind a bookcase — a trailblazer of SF's cocktail revival.
North Beach's last standing Barbary Coast bar (1907), original mahogany bar and punkah fans; well-dressed bartenders, live jazz and a Free Lunch Friday tradition.
Mission bar from Bourbon & Branch/Beretta alumni — cocktails several steps above the norm in an unpretentious room, with one of the best burgers in the city until midnight.
Mission cocktail bar from the Michelin-starred Lazy Bear team; inventive drinks using fermented honey and roasted quince, and North America's 50 Best 'most sustainable bar'.
Award-winning Union Square bar led by local legend Kevin Diedrich; Asian-Pacific-driven drinks that landed it at #16 on North America's 50 Best Bars.

places.w: Inner Richmond bakery named Bon Appetit's Bakery of the Year; preposterously flaky, brioche-tender croissants that draw a daily line — widely called SF's best.
Lower Pac Heights French patisserie from James Beard-winning pastry chef Belinda Leong; the caramel-crusted kouign-amann is considered among the country's best.
Outer Sunset beach-side bakery selling 500-600 breakfast sandwiches a weekend — egg, pepper jack, bacon, avocado and lemon-garlic aioli on a buttermilk biscuit; pillowy $1 Sunday beignets.

13-time World Pizza Champion Tony Gemignani's flagship; ranked #3 pizza in the U.S. by 50 Top Pizza. 12 styles cooked in seven ovens — the Neapolitan Margherita (limited daily) and the coal-fired New Yorker are the ones to get.

Punk-rock North Beach institution since 1978; airy focaccia squares with an impeccably crunchy bottom, sold by the slice. The clam & garlic and the sausage combo are the classics — line out the door, takeout only.
Gold-medal Italian deli since 1896, one of the oldest in the U.S. House-cured Molinari salami piled on Dutch-crunch — a legendary counter sandwich by Washington Square.
Family-run since 1937, overlooking Washington Square. The originator of the Joe's Special — a mayor-proclaimed San Francisco classic — plus reliable red-sauce pasta and steaks in an old-school room.

Iconic 1919 North Beach bar-restaurant revived by Anna Weinberg, chef Nancy Oakes and Ken Fulk. Go for the scene, the Tosca meatballs, and the boozy house 'cappuccino' (armagnac and bourbon, no espresso).
VPN-certified wood-fired Neapolitan pies (Caputo flour, DOP San Marzano) plus a mozzarella bar of imported bufala and burrata. Time Out rates it 5/5; the broccoli & salsiccia is the pick.
A North Beach red-sauce holdout tracing to 1906 (celebrated its 110th year in 2016). Old-school family-recipe pastas and a convivial, checkered-tablecloth room on Green St.

places.w: Michelin-starred SF institution since 1999 near the Wharf. Build a multi-course tasting around signatures like glazed oysters with lettuce cream and osetra, and herb-crusted loin of lamb.
James Beard Best New Restaurant (2013) and Michelin-starred. Dim-sum-style carts roll New American small plates — the namesake quail and the cheesy sauerkraut pancakes are essential.

Michelin Bib Gourmand (2023) — a contemporary Korean sharing-menu that folds in parmesan and chorizo alongside classics like mulhwe (raw seafood in chilled fermented-chili broth) and crackling lime-soy fried chicken.
James Beard Outstanding Restaurant winner and Michelin-listed; Judy Rodgers' brick-oven roast chicken for two over warm bread salad has been the city's defining Cal-cuisine dish since 1979.
The Divisadero gathering place that named a neighborhood; organic wood-fired California cooking whose pork chop is routinely called the best in the city, with bubbling wood-baked beans alongside.
Hayes Valley's inventive Californian star (former Michelin star; #3 on the SF Chronicle Top 100, 2025). The sardine-threaded potato chips with horseradish dip are the signature opener.
Chef Kim Alter's intimate Hayes Valley tasting-menu room behind a carved-owl door; a tightly orchestrated seasonal menu (dry-aged squab with cabbage and mole) with the Linden Room bar next door.

places.w: James Beard-nominated Gayle Pirie and John Clark's California-Mediterranean landmark since 1999; oysters and sesame-curry fried chicken, with foreign films projected on the patio wall at dusk.

Melissa Perello's Michelin-recognized Castro bistro since 2010 — a refined but neighborly French-leaning California menu that changes daily; the closest clean fill for the French gap now that the classic French rooms have shuttered.
The Mission's iconic hand-churned creamery by Dolores Park (since 2006); the salted-caramel and coffee-toffee ice-cream sandwiches draw a line around the block.

James Beard-nominated Heena Patel's regional Gujarati cooking inside the Minnesota Street Project in Dogpatch; California-inflected home dishes like malai kofta, blue-cheese naan and fire-charred eggplant with garlic confit.
Mourad Lahlou's Richmond restaurant — the first Moroccan restaurant in the U.S. to earn a Michelin star (2010) — reimagining Moroccan cooking with California produce; the golden basteeya is the icon.

Elevated to three Michelin stars in the 2026 California guide (sfist, 2026-06-25).

The city's definitive upscale Greek room in Jackson Square — open-hearth grill and wood oven perfuming a fireplace-lit dining room; grilled lamb chops, moussaka and some of the best grilled octopus in town.
Michelin-starred, live-fire seafood from Saison Hospitality on the Embarcadero waterfront; embered oysters with smoked chili butter and a steak-knife radicchio salad, cooked over an open hearth.

Suzette Gresham's two-Michelin-star Italian fine-dining room in a converted chapel on Nob Hill; house-made pastas, seasonal truffle risotto, and the signature ridged pasta with faux foie gras and truffle.

Michelin Bib Gourmand — the Bay Area's modern Filipino tasting-menu counter from chef Patrick Gabon; fermentation-driven takes like braised-gizzard sisig on brioche pandesal and dry-aged duck-breast adobo, 10-12 seats at a single counter. Earned its first Michelin star in the 2026 guide.
The original Swensen's, opened 1948 at Hyde & Union on the Russian Hill cable-car line and the last U.S. parlor of the name — over 100 flavors churned old-school on the corner.
The definitive Mission burrito since 1973 — no rice, seared meat, lines down the block. The carne asada super burrito is the one to get.
Infatuation names it SF's best burrito outright — a nearly two-pound super burrito with charred carne asada and ideal ratios of guac, cheese, crema. Open since 1983.
Classic Mission taqueria; the carnitas burrito mojado doused in red chili with red and green salsa is big enough to split.
